# `useless-error-return`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: correctness · Profile: none · Default: warning · Fixes: none · Options: none

Reports a fully visible function body that cannot fail although its signature
returns an error union.
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

An unearned error union makes every caller handle a failure that cannot occur
and misstates the function's contract.

## When it fires

The rule stays silent for exported functions and any body containing
propagation, error construction, calls, catches, or potentially fallible
builtins. It reports only inferred error sets (`!T`): a named one (`Error!T`,
`error{A}!T`) is a contract the function fulfils, and so is the signature of a
function in an anonymous struct passed as an argument or accessed in place
(`struct { fn f() ... }.f`), which its receiver sets. Removing the error channel is an API decision, so no fix-all edit is
offered.

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
fn answer() !u32 {
    return 42;
}
```
